summary: Run optional Transform _flush after written input is consumed and before readable end.

target.notes: Call flush only after no more written data remains, allow zero or more final pushes, require callback completion, then permit readable end. On error, normal end/finish must not be synthesized incorrectly.

semantics.timing: after all transform input, before readable end

caveats: Application code must not call _flush directly.
Writable finish and readable end are related but distinct sides of Transform lifecycle.

tests.name: flush emits trailing data
tests.input: const {Transform}=require('node:stream'); const t=new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){cb(null,c)},flush(cb){this.push('!');cb()}}); let s=''; t.on('data',c=>s+=c); t.on('end',()=>console.log(s)); t.end('a');

tests.name: flush precedes end
tests.input: const {Transform}=require('node:stream'); const out=[]; const t=new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){cb()},flush(cb){out.push('flush');cb()}}); t.on('end',()=>{out.push('end');console.log(out.join(','))}); t.resume(); t.end();
